b1-unit-14.14.1 Dinner is on me:
Danny: So, this is the place. Bruno says it's the best Bahian food in São Paulo.
Ana: It smells amazing. And you look much better than last week!
Danny: I feel great. That's why we're here. You were my doctor, so tonight dinner is on me.
Waiter: Good evening. Are you ready to order, or do you need a few more minutes?
Danny: I think we're ready. Could you tell me what's in the moqueca? I've never had it.
Waiter: Of course. It's a fish stew made with coconut milk, tomatoes, onions, peppers and palm oil. It's cooked slowly in a clay pot.
Danny: And do you know if it's very spicy? I'm not great with hot food.
Waiter: It's not spicy at all. We serve the hot pepper sauce on the side.
Danny: Perfect. What does it come with?
Waiter: It's served with white rice, pirão and farofa.
Danny: That sounds fine. I'll have the moqueca, then.
Waiter: Very good. And for you, ma'am?
Ana: I'd like to start with two acarajés as an appetizer, to share. And for my main course, I'll have the shrimp bobó.
Waiter: Excellent choice. Anything to drink?
Danny: I'll have a coconut water. No, wait... make that a passion fruit juice.
Ana: Just water for me, please. Sparkling, if you have it.
Waiter: Certainly.
Danny: Ana, do you know what pirão is? I didn't want to ask.
Ana: It's a kind of thick sauce made with fish broth and cassava flour. You'll love it.
Waiter: Did you enjoy your meal? Can I get you some dessert? I can recommend the cocada. It's homemade.
Ana: No, thanks. I'm completely full. I don't think I have room for anything else.
Danny: Me too. Could we have the check, please?
Waiter: Of course. Just a moment.
Ana: Let me get this, Danny. You're on a gap year!
Danny: No, no. It's on me. You saved my life last week.
Ana: You had the flu, Danny. You didn't need saving! But OK, if you insist. Next time is on me.
Danny: Deal. Hey, the check says ten percent service. Do you know if I should leave a tip too?
Ana: In Brazil, that ten percent is the tip. It's optional, but people usually pay it when the service is good.
Danny: The service was great. I'll pay it. Back home, my mom always leaves twenty percent!
